info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package usage is what your org ran and what it cost, broken down per account.

post.summary: Ingests a batch of account-usage samples — what a developer's OWN AI accounts have consumed of their OWN plans, metered from each provider's own login — and appends them to the warehouse series.
post.description:
Ingests a batch of account-usage samples — what a developer's OWN AI
accounts have consumed of their OWN plans, metered from each provider's own
login — and appends them to the warehouse series. Answers 202.

Send either a `samples` array or one sample's fields at the top level. Every
sample needs a provider, a machine and a known window class; an unknown window or
kind is refused rather than silently rewritten, because a dash filled with a class
nobody reported is worse than an error. There is no timestamp field: the server
owns the observation clock, and a sample says which window it measured with
windowStart or resetsAt.

It is FAIL-SOFT on storage: a warehouse outage costs a poll of history
(stored:false), never a failed request. It records usage ONLY — the link registry
is refreshed separately via POST /v1/links, so there is one and only one way to
update an account row.

get.summary: Is the entitlement-GATED per-provider breakdown of the caller org's LLM usage — the paid lens over the same warehouse ledger GET /v1/usage/summary reads its totals from.
get.description:
Is the entitlement-GATED per-provider breakdown of the caller org's LLM
usage — the paid lens over the same warehouse ledger GET /v1/usage/summary reads
its totals from. Basic own-org usage stays ungated at /v1/usage/summary.

A plan that does not grant the analytics datastore is refused with 402, and an
unresolvable plan fails closed to the free floor, which does not grant it. The
window is clamped forward to the plan's retention entitlement, so a tenant can
never read older than its plan allows even with a custom start. The response is
marked no-store.

INTERIM (mirrors apps/world's limits echo): no org→plan resolver exists in cloud
yet — the subscription lookup is owned by the billing plane and the gateway
principal carries no plan claim — so the caller passes the plan and the gate
resolves THAT plan's access.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End is the exclusive window end, RFC3339. Read only when Range is custom.

parameters.name: plan
parameters.description:
Plan is the plan id whose entitlement decides access and retention. INTERIM:
cloud has no org-to-plan resolver yet, so the caller names the plan; when
that resolver lands this becomes the caller org's own plan.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is the window: a count and a unit — 24h, 7d, 90d, any <N>h or <N>d —
or day, week, month, all, custom. Empty means 24h. The window is then
clamped forward to the plan's retention entitlement.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Start is the inclusive window start, RFC3339. Read only when Range is
custom, and clamped forward to the plan's retention floor.

get.summary: Echoes a plan's resolved analytics entitlement so a dashboard can configure itself against the LIVE catalog instead of hardcoding tier numbers.
get.description:
Echoes a plan's resolved analytics entitlement so a dashboard can
configure itself against the LIVE catalog instead of hardcoding tier numbers. An
empty plan resolves the free floor, and a catalog resolution failure serves that
same floor rather than erroring — so this always answers 200. It is a read-only
contract echo and carries no tenant data.

parameters.name: plan
parameters.description:
Plan is a plan id from the live @hanzo/plans catalog. Empty resolves the
free floor, and so does an id the catalog does not know — this never fails
on an unknown plan.

get.summary: Is the PER-PROVIDER view: one connected account's own consumption of its own plan — "my plan is 47% through its 6h window, resets at 14:20".
get.description:
Is the PER-PROVIDER view: one connected account's own consumption of its
own plan — "my plan is 47% through its 6h window, resets at 14:20".

`current` is the newest instance of each lane (the headline); `windows` is the
history behind it. Both come from ONE deduped read, so they can never disagree.
The rows are the caller's OWN linked accounts, scoped to the validated principal
and its subject — never another user's, and never another org's.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description:
Account narrows to ONE linked account of that provider. Empty covers every
account the caller has linked there.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider is the upstream to read, e.g. anthropic. Required.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is the window to read: a count and a unit — 1h, 24h, 90d, any <N>h or
<N>d — or day, week, month, all. Empty means 24h. A label that is not a
count, or one reaching past the 730-day horizon, is refused rather than
silently replaced.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description:
Window narrows to ONE window class: 6h, day, week or month. Empty covers
every class.

get.summary: Answers GET /v1/usage/summary: the caller's own usage footprint over one window — the categorized spend roll-up from the commerce ledger, the org's LLM usage totals from the warehouse, and the caller's OWN linked provider accounts beside the org's Hanzo-routed usage.
get.description:
Answers GET /v1/usage/summary: the caller's own usage footprint over one
window — the categorized spend roll-up from the commerce ledger, the org's LLM
usage totals from the warehouse, and the caller's OWN linked provider accounts
beside the org's Hanzo-routed usage.

Every source degrades INDEPENDENTLY to honest zeros and says so in `sources` and
in its own `available` flag, so a partial deploy reports "no data" rather than
fabricating spend. The account rows and the Hanzo rows are concatenated and never
summed: a plan's percent is not money.

The response is org-scoped from the validated principal and marked no-store — a
signed-out caller is refused.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is the window: a count and a unit — 24h, 7d, 90d, any <N>h or <N>d —
or day, week, month, all, custom. Empty means 24h. A label this surface
does not know, or one reaching past the 730-day horizon, is refused rather
than silently replaced.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Start is the inclusive window start, RFC3339. Read only when Range is
custom.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End is the exclusive window end, RFC3339. Read only when Range is custom.

account.description: Account is the state of the caller's own linked-account side.

hanzo.description: Hanzo is the state of the org's Hanzo-routed side.

rows.description:
Rows is the two row sets CONCATENATED, never summed — each row says which
side it came from. A percent is not money and a provider's own spend is not
a Hanzo charge, so adding them would produce a number that means nothing.

category.description:
Category is the bucket the ledger's own tag mapped to. An untagged or
unrecognised line gets its own honest bucket rather than being folded away.

cents.description: Cents is what the org spent in that bucket over the window, in US cents.

count.description: Count is how many ledger lines rolled up into it.

available.description:
Available is false when the warehouse was not connected or a query blipped.
The totals below are then honest zeros, NOT measured ones.

costCents.description: CostCents is what they cost the org, in US cents. This IS a Hanzo charge.

models.description: Models is how many distinct models were used.

promptTokens.description: PromptTokens is the input half of that total.

requests.description: Requests is how many completions the org made in the window.

source.description: Source names the warehouse table the totals came from.

tokens.description: Tokens is the total tokens those completions consumed.

available.description:
Available is false when the warehouse could not be read, which means "no
answer" and NOT "no usage" — Items is then empty for a reason.

items.description: Items is one row per provider, most tokens first.

source.description: Source names the warehouse table the rows came from.

costCents.description: CostCents is what they cost the org, in US cents.

provider.description: Provider is the upstream the requests were routed to, e.g. anthropic.

requests.description: Requests is how many completions the org made against that provider.

tokens.description:
Tokens is the total tokens those completions consumed, prompt plus
completion.

available.description:
Available is whether this side's ledger answered. False means its rows are
missing, not that there were none.

note.description:
Note is the human sentence that says what this side's numbers mean, so a
board cannot present a plan percentage as a Hanzo charge.

scope.description: Scope is whose rows this side carries: "user" or "org".

source.description: Source is the table of record the rows came from.

commerce.description: Commerce is whether the billing ledger answered the spend block.

warehouse.description: Warehouse is whether the usage warehouse answered the LLM block.

available.description:
Available is false when the commerce ledger was unconfigured or
unreachable. Every number below is then an honest zero, NOT a measured one.

availableCents.description: AvailableCents is what of that balance is still spendable.

balanceCents.description: BalanceCents is the prepaid wallet's balance, in US cents.

byCategory.description: ByCategory is the window's spend split by ledger category, largest first.

mtdCents.description:
MTDCents is commerce's authoritative month-to-date consumed figure, which
is a different period from the window and is not derived from it.

overageCents.description: OverageCents is month-to-date consumption beyond the plan's allowance.

series.description:
Series is the window's spend over time, gap-filled at the window's
interval.

source.description: Source names where the roll-up came from.

totalCents.description:
TotalCents is consumption over the requested window, in US cents. It is
self-consistent with ByCategory and Series.

cents.description: Cents is the consumption recorded in that bucket, in US cents.

t.description:
T is the bucket's start instant, RFC3339 UTC. Buckets are gap-filled, so a
window with no spend still has its points.

confidence.description:
Confidence says how much the counters mean; a percentage-only meter leaves
them at zero.

costCents.description:
CostCents is the row's cost in US cents. For an "account" row this is the
PROVIDER's own charge, not a Hanzo one.

provider.description: Provider is the upstream the usage was measured against.

requests.description: Requests is how many requests the row covers.

scope.description:
Scope is whose row it is: "user" for the caller's own linked accounts,
"org" for the whole tenant's Hanzo-routed usage.

source.description:
Source is where the row came from: "account" is the provider's own meter
on the caller's linked account, "hanzo" is Hanzo-routed inference. The two
are never summed.

tokens.description: Tokens is the total tokens the row covers.

usedPct.description:
UsedPct is how much of a plan window the row consumed, 0–100. It is a
share, never money.

window.description: Window is the meter window class the row rolls up, when it has one.

windows.description: Windows is how many window instances rolled up into the row.

account.description: Account is the linked account that was asked about, when one was named.

available.description:
Available is false when the warehouse could not be read. That means "no
answer", NOT "no usage" — the two lists below are then empty for a reason.

current.description: Current is the newest window instance of each lane — the dash headline.

from.description: From is the inclusive start of that window, RFC3339 UTC.

provider.description: Provider is the upstream that was asked about, echoed back.

range.description: Range is the window that was served: 1h, 24h, 7d or 30d.

scope.description: Scope says whose rows these are: the caller's own linked accounts.

source.description: Source names the meter of record — the provider's own login, not Hanzo.

to.description: To is the exclusive end of that window, RFC3339 UTC.

windows.description: Windows is every instance in range, newest first — the history behind it.

account.description: Account is the linked account the window was metered from.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens the provider served from cache.

confidence.description: Confidence says how much the counters below mean.

costCents.description: CostCents is what the window cost on the PROVIDER's own plan, in US cents.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.

currency.description: Currency is the provider's currency when it is not US cents.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is prompt tokens consumed in the window.

kind.description:
Kind is subscription or apikey. Empty is accepted; anything else is
refused.

lane.description: Lane is the meter lane within the account.

machine.description: Machine is the host whose meter read the window. Required on every sample.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is completion tokens produced in the window.

plan.description: Plan is the subscription plan the account is on, as the provider names it.

provider.description:
Provider is the upstream the account belongs to, e.g. anthropic. Required
on every sample.

requests.description: Requests is how many requests the window covers.

resetsAt.description: ResetsAt is when the measured window rolls over, RFC3339.

samples.description:
Samples is the batch form: every lane a poller measured, in one call. When
it is non-empty the top-level sample fields are ignored.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a window the meter inferred rather than read.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total tokens.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, 0–100.

window.description:
Window is the window class: 6h, day, week or month. Required, and a class
this surface does not know is refused rather than rewritten.

windowMinutes.description:
WindowMinutes is the window's real length in minutes, as the meter reports
it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC3339. This is how a
backfill states WHICH window it measured; the server always owns the
observation clock, so there is no timestamp field.

accepted.description:
Accepted is how many samples passed validation. Every one of them was
accepted, or the whole report was refused — there is no partial success.

stored.description:
Stored is whether the warehouse actually persisted them. False means the
datastore was unavailable and the poll of history was lost; the request
still succeeded, so a device retries without being blocked.

account.description: Account is the linked account the window was metered from.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens the provider served from cache.

confidence.description: Confidence says how much the counters below mean.

costCents.description: CostCents is what the window cost on the PROVIDER's own plan, in US cents.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.

currency.description: Currency is the provider's currency when it is not US cents.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is prompt tokens consumed in the window.

kind.description:
Kind is subscription or apikey. Empty is accepted; anything else is
refused.

lane.description: Lane is the meter lane within the account.

machine.description: Machine is the host whose meter read the window. Required.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is completion tokens produced in the window.

plan.description: Plan is the subscription plan the account is on, as the provider names it.

provider.description: Provider is the upstream the account belongs to, e.g. anthropic. Required.

requests.description: Requests is how many requests the window covers.

resetsAt.description:
ResetsAt is when the measured window rolls over, RFC3339. Empty is
allowed; anything else that is not RFC3339 is refused.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a window the meter inferred rather than read.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total tokens.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, 0–100.

window.description:
Window is the window class: 6h, day, week or month. Required, and a class
this surface does not know is refused rather than rewritten.

windowMinutes.description:
WindowMinutes is the window's real length in minutes, as the meter reports
it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC3339. Empty is allowed;
anything else that is not RFC3339 is refused.

access.description: Access is what that plan grants.

plan.description: Plan echoes the plan id that was resolved, exactly as it was asked for.

datastore.description:
Datastore is whether the plan may read GET /v1/usage/analytics at all. The
free floor is false, and that is what a catalog outage resolves to.

export.description: Export is whether the plan may export the analytics it can read.

retentionDays.description:
RetentionDays is how far back the plan may read. GET /v1/usage/analytics
clamps a custom window's start to this, so an older `start` returns the
clamped window rather than an error.

end.description: End is the window's exclusive end, RFC3339 UTC.

export.description: Export is whether the resolved plan allows exporting these rows.

plan.description: Plan echoes the plan id the entitlement was resolved from.

providers.description: Providers is the per-provider roll-up over the window.

range.description:
Range is the label that was ASKED for. A plan whose retention is shorter
than that window is served the retention instead, so read start and end for
the window the rows actually cover and retentionDays for the reason — on a
clamped read the label is longer than what was served.

retentionDays.description: RetentionDays is how far back the resolved plan allows reading.

scope.description: Scope is the tenant the rows were read under — the validated principal's org.

start.description:
Start is the window's inclusive start, RFC3339 UTC, AFTER the retention
clamp — so it may be later than the start that was asked for.

org.description:
Org is the IAM org slug the rows were read under — the validated
principal's, never a client header.

user.description:
User is the caller's own subject, whose linked-account rows the accounts
block carries. Absent on a read that is org-scoped only.

accounts.description:
Accounts is the caller's own linked provider accounts beside the org's
Hanzo-routed usage, labelled row by row and never summed together.

end.description: End is the window's exclusive end, RFC3339 UTC.

interval.description: Interval is the bucket width the spend series is gap-filled at.

llm.description: LLM is the org's Hanzo-routed inference totals from the warehouse.

range.description: Range is the window label that was served.

scope.description: Scope is the tenant and subject the roll-up was answered for.

sources.description:
Sources says which upstreams actually answered, so a zero can be read as
"no data yet" rather than as a measurement.

spend.description: Spend is the categorized cost roll-up from the billing ledger.

start.description: Start is the window's inclusive start, RFC3339 UTC.

account.description: Account is the linked provider account the window belongs to.

cachedInputTokens.description:
CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens served from the provider's cache;
omitted when unknown.

confidence.description:
Confidence says how much the counters beside it mean — a meter that
reported only a percentage leaves them at zero, and this is how a reader
tells that from a true zero.

costCents.description:
CostCents is what the window cost on the PROVIDER's own plan, in US cents.
It is not a Hanzo charge.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.

currency.description: Currency is the provider's currency when it is not US cents.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is prompt tokens consumed in the window; omitted when unknown.

lane.description:
Lane is the meter lane this instance belongs to, e.g. a provider's own
rolling-window meter.

machine.description: Machine is the host whose meter reported the window.

outputTokens.description:
OutputTokens is completion tokens produced in the window; omitted when
unknown.

plan.description: Plan is the subscription plan the account is on, as the provider names it.

requests.description:
Requests is how many requests were made in the window; omitted when the
meter did not report it.

resetsAt.description: ResetsAt is when this window rolls over, RFC3339 UTC; omitted when unknown.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks an instance the meter inferred rather than read.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total tokens; omitted when unknown.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, 0–100.

window.description: Window is the window class: 6h, day, week or month.

windowMinutes.description:
WindowMinutes is the window's real length in minutes when the meter
reported one; omitted when it did not.

windowStart.description: WindowStart is when this window opened, RFC3339 UTC; omitted when unknown.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
